title: Dense open Bruhat cell for the longest Weyl element
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $G$ a reductive $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], meaning a smooth connected affine group scheme of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq G$, a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$, its unipotent radical $U$, and the positive roots $\Phi^+$, with these notions as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Let $N_G(T)$ be the subgroup scheme of $G$ normalizing $T$, and let $W=N_G(T)(F)/T(F)$ act on $X^*(T)$ by $(w\chi)(t)=\chi(n^{-1}tn)$ for a representative $n\in N_G(T)(F)$. There is a unique element $w_0\in W$ such that $w_0(\Phi^+)=-\Phi^+$. For every representative $n_0\in N_G(T)(F)$ of $w_0$, the morphism of $F$-schemes
$$j:U\times_F B\longrightarrow G,\qquad (u,b)\longmapsto u n_0 b$$
is an open immersion with dense topological image [def-weil-open-immersion]; thus it identifies $U\times_F B$ with a dense open subscheme of $G$. The trivial group and rank-zero case are allowed.

source.place: Definition 21.72, Theorem 21.73(b), Theorem 21.84 and Definition 21.85, printed pp.447--451; the map (u,b) to u n_0 b is stated explicitly in the proof of Proposition 22.22, printed pp.468--469.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts] to the given $F,G,T,B$, writing its $V$ as our $U$. Its hypotheses are exactly the reductive Borel-pair hypotheses in the statement. It gives the unique $w_0$ reversing $\Phi^+$. Choose its system of representatives and write $n_*$ for the representative of $w_0$. Its multiplication isomorphism for $w=w_0$, together with $V^{w_0}=V$, is an isomorphism $k:U\times_F B\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{w_0}$, $k(u,b)=u n_* b$, where $C_{w_0}$ is an open dense subscheme of $G$.

Let $n_0$ be any representative of $w_0$. Equality of their classes in $N_G(T)(F)/T(F)$ gives $t\in T(F)\subseteq B(F)$ with $n_0=n_*t$. The morphism $a_t:U\times_F B\to U\times_F B$, $(u,b)\mapsto(u,tb)$, has inverse $a_{t^{-1}}$ by the group-scheme multiplication and unit identities. Thus $k\circ a_t$ is an isomorphism onto the same $C_{w_0}$, with inverse $a_{t^{-1}}\circ k^{-1}$. As morphisms of schemes its composite with $C_{w_0}\hookrightarrow G$ sends $(u,b)$ to $u n_*(tb)=u n_0 b$; this is the required $j$. The identities hold on points over every $F$-algebra, including nonreduced algebras.

source.place: Theorem 21.80(b) and proof of Proposition 22.22, printed pp.450,468--469; elementary change of representative written out.

proof.text: By [def-weil-open-immersion], an isomorphism onto an open subscheme followed by its inclusion is an open immersion. The preceding explicit isomorphism therefore makes $j$ an open immersion with image $|C_{w_0}|$. This image is dense by step 1, giving all the assertions. No positive rank or nonempty root set was used: the cited chart theorem applies also when $\Phi$ is empty, so the same specialization and inverse apply to tori and to the trivial group.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q07-6bb991bf6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS, no changes. The delivery is one commit: the item, now split, plus its report. It adds no new nodes, and the statement, stmt_deps and source are unchanged. proof_deps are exactly the union of the step citations. Live and side-live still have the item unsplit, and no repair note applies. Step 1 cites the existing same-unit node lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts (Q158, on the base). Its statement strictly contains the item: unique w_0; scheme isomorphisms V^w x B -> C_w, (u,b) -> u n_w b; C_{w_0} open dense; V^{w_0}=V. Citing it instead of creating a duplicate is correct under C5. Neither cited node's dependency closure reaches the item, so there is no cycle. Step 2 is elementary and correct: n_0 = n_* t with t in T(F) inside B(F), a_t(u,b)=(u,tb) is an automorphism, and k∘a_t = j on A-points for every F-algebra A. Step 3 applies the 'equivalently' clause of def-weil-open-immersion, and density comes from step 1. Sources checked in the local Milne iAG PDF: Def 21.72, Thm 21.73(b), Thm 21.80(b) (U^w x B -> U^w n_w B is an isomorphism), Def 21.85 (big cell = B_u w_0 B), and the proof of Prop 22.22, which states that U x B -> G, (u,b) -> u w_0 b, is an open immersion. Edge cases checked: the torus and trivial group (Phi empty, j is a translation), and SL_2, where the image is D(g_21) and the U n_0 B orientation matches Milne. There are no SGA citations and no tool_uses. The report mentions a citations.json that is not in the commit; this is harmless.
